saints.name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
saints.title: Patroness of the Americas
saints.shortBlurb: The Mother of God, appearing on the hill of Tepeyac and leaving her image on a poor man's cloak, drew a whole people to Christ…
biography: In December 1531, ten years after the Spanish conquest of Mexico, the Mother of God appeared four times on the hill of Tepeyac to Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin, an Indian convert on his way to Mass, speaking to him in his own Nahuatl tongue and asking that a church be built on that spot in her honor.

The bishop of Mexico, the Franciscan Juan de Zumárraga, asked for a sign. On 12 December the Virgin sent Juan Diego to gather Castilian roses blooming out of season on the stony hill, and when he opened his cactus-fiber cloak before the bishop, out fell the roses, and upon the cloak appeared her image — the tilma venerated ever since as Our Lady of Guadalupe.

The image drew multitudes of the native peoples to baptism, and the shrine at Tepeyac grew into the most visited Marian sanctuary in the world. Pius XII proclaimed her Queen of Mexico and Empress of the Americas in 1945, and John Paul II canonized the seer Juan Diego in 2002, the first indigenous saint of the Americas.
saints.knownFor: Her apparition at Tepeyac and the miraculous image on the tilma.
